# Sacca Saṁyutta (SN 56)

**ID:** SN 56  
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Sacca Saṁyutta  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul11.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul11.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 Unlike the Pāli placement in the *Mahāvagga*, the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* assigns the *Satya-saṁyukta* to the *Nidānavagga* [Bodhi 2000]. Individual discourses, such as the *Papātasutta* (SN 56.42) and *Mahāpariḷāhasutta* (SN 56.43), warn of the dire consequences of ignorance of the truths and find parallels in the Gāndhārī Senior scroll collection (Senior 8) and Sanskrit fragments [Marino 2017]. An early North Indian inscription from the 2nd–3rd century CE also quotes the four noble truths, likely drawing from this collection [Winternitz 1933].
